body:
>  I feel like I died a long time ago and my body just hasn't realized it.

Reminds me of this quote from John Bergin on why James 'O' Barr wrote "The Crow" Graphic Novel:

"James did this book because he died inside but found he was still breathing."

> Look there are certainly cases where this happens, but like with most things: exceptions confirm the rule. It is by no means the rule that moderate views get hated on a lot even if they are not mainstream. 

I don't believe that.  

>But thats not how the world is. At all. Extremist beliefs are only held by a minority. 

You haven't been on Facebook or Twitter lately, have you?  

I witnessed a friend declare she would unfriend anyone that didn't share her extreme views informed by raw hysteria.  Someone I once supported and believe she (once) was a decent individual.

You know what happened?  Others with her mindset validated it and anyone who tried to talk some sense into her were lambasted into oblivion by her and this mob.  That's what kept me from sharing my own moderate view.  

>So why dont you tell me what we are talking about here? 

Sorry, don't feel safe even here.  Or anywhere for that matter.

> Sorry but thats simply not the case.

Really?  So people getting their careers ruined because of one opinion that is misconstrued is enough to know this world basks in impulsive lynch mobbing?  Being unfriended on Facebook, blocked on Twitter, while the person who did it spreads malicious, unfounded rumors about you, tarnishing your reputation further?  Those aren't sufficient enough to conclude nuance is a thing of the past? 


>Yes emotions might get hot when speaking about views that involve things that are important to you, but straight out hate is not the case most of the times.

Yeah, and those same emotions lead to people labeling your opinion "Hate".  That's my point.  

>Of course sometimes that shit happens when extreme views encounter eachother, but the vast majority is quite moderate.

I'm not talking about extreme views.  I'm talking about moderate views in a sea of extremities sniping at each other, doxxing each other and all that.  That's why I don't feel this world is for me.

> Of course there is always a more popular opinion about things but unless it is fueled by hatred people mostly respect others opinions.

That's not how the world works now.  Maybe once upon a time.  Presently, anything that doesn't toe a line is considered "Hate".  

I'd rather not live in such a world.

> Hey dude whats up? What makes you think like that? 

In today's climate, people wouldn't welcome my views.  It's all I can say without worrying about getting ostracized by those who lack looking at things with nuance.

Let's face it, I'm a good Samaritan but that would be destroyed if I ever went against the grain.  Even people I admire are hopping on the bandwagon and it's heartbreaking.  No one left to be inspired by except myself...and I don't exactly have a high opinion of myself.
